items.item: upgrading a table to v3 initializes next-row-id to 0; existing snapshots' row-id fields read as null
equality deletes break row lineage: the reinserted row gets a brand-new _row_id, not the original, since the writer never reads the existing row
start-snapshot-id is exclusive, end-snapshot-id is inclusive, and the latter defaults to the current snapshot if omitted

change data files follow the table's retention policy; VACUUM deletes them

The row-lineage model in examples.py is a from-scratch Python implementation of the v3 spec's actual rules (next-row-id counter, when _last_updated_sequence_number resets vs carries forward), not a wrapper around a real Iceberg catalog or Spark session, which this sandbox cannot run, disclosed in the script's own docstring and FACT-CHECK.md red-team #1.

The naive-vs-lineage scan distinction matches create_changelog_view's own documented carry-over example (file holding two rows, deleting one forces the other into a new file, reported as a spurious delete+insert pair) scaled up to 10 and 20 rows, per FACT-CHECK.md red-team #2.
